newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Fantasy Fest rule body paint is not clothing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Fantasy Fest rule body paint is not clothing.

text.p: For the 50,000 revellers expected at this year's oft-controversial Fantasy Fest, a thin veneer of acrylic paint will no longer qualify as clothing.

Police say it is not a crackdown, but the body painting law and the confinement of public drinking to a 10-block "fantasy zone" along the main tourist drag are the latest attempts to rein in Key West's annual walk on the wild side.

With new rules firmly in place, the festival of the bizarre in this southernmost U.S. town began on Friday with nine days of costumes and parties culminating in a parade down historic Duval Street on the Saturday before Halloween.

Fantasy Fest was begun in 1979 by a group of local business people determined to lure tourists during the slow time before the traditional winter season. Fundamentalist Christians have long opposed the festival, in part because it has been known as a gay event featuring public nudity.
One of its highlights is the annual coronation of the Fantasy Fest king and queen. As longtime organiser Ann Dickinson puts it: "We've had kings who have been queens and queens who have been kings."

Key Westers like to say the 18-year-old event is their answer to the freewheeling New Orleans Mardi Gras party, but this year the preparations were anything but freewheeling thanks to the Monroe County Christian Coalition.

The group launched an all-out offensive against Fantasy Fest, calling it a week of "depravity and debauchery." The city commission listened, but appeared determined to curb the revelry without scaring away the tourist dollars.

The commission's biggest concession was to ban the popular practice of body painting, where artists use naked human beings as canvas to create everything from false bikinis to twisted faces with breasts for eyes.
The city commission passed the ordinance in June despite protests by painters, who said a layer of paint constituted clothing.
Keys Bible School Pastor Bill Welzien, a member of the Christian Coalition, said the ordinance was a start but would do little to cure the raunchy excess of Fantasy Fest.
Few expect vigorous enforcement of the nude painting ordinance by the Key West police, who seem determined to avoid the appearance of a crackdown.

"Persons exposing private body parts, including women exposing their breasts, will be asked by police to cover themselves or leave the streets immediately," according to a statement from the Police Department. Failing that, violators could be arrested for disorderly conduct.
